title: Lily and Ben's Big Radio Day

pages.title: Lily Gets Her Call Sign
pages.text: Lily studied hard, and today she passed her ham radio test! Now she has her very own call sign: a special name made of letters and numbers that only she can use on the air. She sits at her radio desk with her new headphones. Pickles the cat naps on top of the warm radio. On the wall is a map of the United States, so Lily can color in every state she talks to. And on the desk is her radio log, ready for her very first contact.

pages.title: Off to the Park
pages.text: On Saturday, Lily, her dad and her dog Scout drive to a Kentucky state park. Lily is going to do Parks on the Air! That means talking on the radio from a park so other hams can "hunt" it. They set up the tent, a folding chair and a little table. Dad helps her raise the antenna pole and tie it down with ropes so the wind can't knock it over. A sign points every way: Parks, Trails, Explore, Learn, Ham Radio and Have Fun. Lily wants to do all of them.

pages.title: Calling CQ
pages.text: Lily puts on her headphones and turns the big knob to find a quiet spot. First she listens, then asks, "Is this frequency in use?" Nobody answers, so it's hers! She presses the button on her microphone and says, "CQ Parks on the Air! This is Lily, calling from a Kentucky park!" CQ means "calling anyone." For a moment there's only a soft hiss. Then a voice comes back from far away in Ohio: "You're five nine!" That means loud and clear. Scout wags his tail.

pages.title: Writing It Down
pages.text: Soon lots of people are calling Lily at once. Hams call that a pileup! She picks one station at a time and spells their call sign with the phonetic alphabet so nobody gets mixed up: "Whiskey Four Alpha Bravo Charlie." In her radio log she writes down each contact: their call sign, the time, where they are and how loud they were. Scout keeps watch while Lily writes. Every line in the log is a new friend somewhere in the world.

pages.title: Ben Learns Morse Code
pages.text: Across Kentucky, a boy named Ben is practicing at his radio desk. Ben loves Morse code, the beeping language of radio. He taps his key: short beeps are dots and long beeps are dashes. He learned one letter at a time. E is one short beep, T is one long beep, and S is three short beeps. Ben's globe and world map remind him that Morse code can travel all the way around the Earth.

pages.title: A Day at the Lake
pages.text: That same Saturday, Ben and his grandpa take his radio to a park by the lake. Grandpa sets up a special antenna on a tall pole. Ben slips on his headphones and slowly turns the dial, listening carefully. Through the hiss he hears a voice calling, "CQ Parks on the Air, from a Kentucky park!" Ben's eyes get big. He knows that voice. It's his friend Lily!

pages.title: Park to Park!
pages.text: Ben grabs his microphone. "Lily, this is Ben, calling from a park too! Park to park!" When both stations are in parks, it's called a park-to-park contact, and hams love them. They give each other a signal report, "You're five nine!", and trade their park numbers. Ben's dog Rusty barks happily, like he knows something exciting just happened.

pages.title: Seventy-Three, Friends!
pages.text: Back home, Ben writes the contact in his log and gives a big thumbs up. Before they signed off, Lily and Ben both said "Seventy-three!" That's radio talk for "best wishes and goodbye." Now Lily and Ben are already planning their next park adventure. Did you know there's no age limit to become a ham radio operator in the United States? Ask a grown-up to help you find a radio club near you. Your call sign could be next! The End.
